skill.name: building-mcp-servers
skill.description: Guides developers through planning, building, testing, and evaluating Model Context Protocol servers in Python or TypeScript.
skill.summary: Build MCP servers with practical patterns for tool design, transports, authentication, testing, and evaluation.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder secrets, and TypeScript template literals. Confirmed risks are concentrated in the evaluation harness, which can launch user-supplied stdio commands and forward secrets, plus documentation that shows broad network exposure settings. No prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Evaluation harness can launch arbitrary stdio commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document that only trusted local MCP servers should be evaluated, and require explicit user approval before running copied commands.

remediation.issue: Examples pass secrets through command-line environment options.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token-looking examples with safer placeholders and recommend secure secret injection that avoids shell history and process listings.

remediation.issue: Transport examples include broad host and network exposure settings.
remediation.suggestion: Default examples to localhost, remove 0.0.0.0 from allowed_hosts, and require authentication plus restrictive CORS for remote deployments.

remediation.issue: Python example shows a tool requesting an API key from the user.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer OAuth, preconfigured environment secrets, or host-managed credentials instead of interactive key collection inside MCP tools.

semantic_findings.title: User-Supplied Command Execution in Evaluation Harness
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation CLI accepts a command and arguments, then passes them to the MCP stdio client. A copied or untrusted command could execute local programs during evaluation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI options define command and args, and the connection class sends them to StdioServerParameters. This is intentional behavior but creates real execution risk if inputs are untrusted.

semantic_findings.title: Secrets Passed Through Command-Line Evaluation Options
semantic_findings.description: The guide demonstrates passing API keys and GitHub tokens through -e command-line options. This can leak secrets through shell history, process listings, or an untrusted child process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation shows concrete -e API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN examples, and the script parses those values. The tokens are placeholders, but the handling pattern is risky.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Remote Transport Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The documentation includes examples with 0.0.0.0 binding, permissive CORS, and broad host allowances. Copying these settings can expose MCP endpoints beyond the intended host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples combine broad network exposure settings with local or internal deployment guidance. This is a real configuration risk even though it is presented as documentation.

semantic_findings.title: Interactive API Key Collection Example
semantic_findings.description: The Python guide shows an MCP tool asking the user for an API key through context elicitation. This pattern can normalize credential collection by tools without a stronger trust flow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly requests sensitive information and then uses it in an API call. It is an example, not malicious code, so the confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires protocol, tool, security, and testing choices. This skill gives practical patterns for Python and TypeScript implementations.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP server planning, tool naming, input schemas, and response design.
Provides Python FastMCP and TypeScript SDK implementation references.
Covers stdio, streamable HTTP, Docker, host validation, and health checks.
Includes guidance for authentication, pagination, errors, annotations, and structured output.
Provides an evaluation harness for testing MCP tools with question and answer files.
Includes a verification script that checks required reference files are present.
limitations: It is for building MCP servers, not for using existing MCP servers.
Examples use placeholder APIs, tokens, and service names that require replacement.
The evaluation harness requires dependencies, a Claude API key, and a trusted MCP server.
Production security settings need review before copying any deployment example.

use_cases.title: Design a New Integration Server
use_cases.description: Plan tools, schemas, transport, authentication, and response formats for a new service integration.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP Implementation Patterns
use_cases.description: Create shared conventions for naming, pagination, error handling, annotations, and deployment.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Tool Quality
use_cases.description: Create evaluation questions and run them against an MCP server to measure task success.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an MCP server for [service]. List the tools, input schemas, outputs, and required authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Service Wrapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [Python or TypeScript] MCP server for [API]. Include validation, pagination, error handling, and structured responses.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP server for tool design, security, validation, transport setup, and agent usability. Prioritize concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Evaluation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Make each answer stable, verifiable, and difficult enough to test tool quality.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output_examples.output: A tool plan with project, task, user, and search operations, plus schemas, annotations, authentication notes, and response formats.

output: Findings about unclear tool names, missing input constraints, weak error messages, and incomplete pagination.
A prioritized fix list with security and usability recommendations.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for a GitHub MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of stable read-only questions with expected answers, verification notes, and guidance for removing destructive tasks.

best_practices: Use strict schemas, clear tool descriptions, and annotations that match real behavior.
Keep secrets in secure configuration and avoid placing tokens in prompts or command history.
Test servers with realistic read-only evaluations before adding write or destructive tools.
anti_patterns: Do not expose local development servers broadly without authentication and host validation.
Do not wrap every API endpoint without designing agent-friendly workflows.
Do not copy placeholder tokens, URLs, or transport settings into production.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build MCP servers that expose service APIs as validated tools for AI agents.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and TypeScript with the MCP SDK.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: It includes helper scripts and reference examples, but most implementation code must be adapted to your service.

faq.question: Can it evaluate an MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an evaluation harness that runs question and answer tests against a trusted MCP server.

faq.question: Is it safe for production deployment?
faq.answer: Use it as guidance only. Review authentication, host binding, CORS, secrets, and transport settings before deployment.

faq.question: Can it consume existing MCP servers?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for building new servers, not for using existing servers directly.
